findings.reason: the `signal-followup-record` implementer is told to merge an existing writer by a name that does not resolve, so the plan must name `persist_mapping_result` (or state a rename) before the node is dispatched.
findings.text: §2 says "`write_mapping_result`'s escalation writer becomes a caller of it", but no function named `write_mapping_result` exists anywhere in `imas_codex/` or `tests/`; the escalation writer that persists `MappingEvidence … evidence_type = 'escalation'` is `persist_mapping_result` (imas_codex/ids/models.py:584), and the same wrong name recurs in §1 (line 38) where it is presented as the existing writer

findings.reason: the mechanism (a `facility.yaml` enum value) only reaches the generated enum through a step the gate command deliberately skips, so the node must add `uv run build-models` (or drop `--no-sync`) or the gate cannot observe the value it asserts.
findings.text: the §2 done-when asserts "an escalation followup round-trips through the generated models" and "the `declared` evidence type accepted", but `imas_codex/graph/models.py` (which carries `class EvidenceType`, line 2468) is gitignored and rebuilt only by the `build-models` hatch sync hook, and the named command is `uv run --no-sync pytest`, which skips that hook

findings.reason: with no declared order between §2 and §4 and a shared write path, a dispatcher can run them concurrently on `ids/models.py` and reach a module before `raise_followup` exists.
findings.text: §4's node `followup-evidence-in-state` writes `imas_codex/ids/models.py` (the same path §2's node writes) and its prose has the conventions stage and the map "raise followups through `raise_followup`", a §2 symbol, yet the node declares only "after `signal-cocos-conventions` §7 and `mapping-decision-chain` §5" — unlike both §3 nodes, which declare "after §2" — and no gate (g-sef-1, g-sef-2) orders it after §2

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §2 (and §1) cite `write_mapping_result` in `imas_codex/ids/models.py`, which resolves to no symbol in the repository; the escalation writer is `persist_mapping_result`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each in-scope node's done-when is a runnable pytest target with a falsifiable assertion, and §3's two nodes carry explicit negative controls (a refused attach with no write; the tool absent in read-only mode).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every in-scope gate is a pytest target under `tests/` in the repository, not a session scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `raise_followup`, `signal_followups`, `EvidenceType.declared` and the node ids are named by what they do, with no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reaching code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2's mechanism adds `declared` to the `EvidenceType` schema, but the done-when pins `--no-sync`, so the schema-derived generated enum the test must observe is never rebuilt.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of `signal-followup-record`, `followup-triage-cli` and `followup-triage-mcp` names one deliverable and one closing verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §4's `followup-evidence-in-state` calls §2's `raise_followup` and shares the write path `imas_codex/ids/models.py` with §2, but declares only external predecessors, so the plan orders no work between them.
